chunks: And he said (peace be upon him)

Sahl ibn Hunayf al-Ansari died in Kufah after his return with him from Siffin, and he was the battle, and he was the most beloved of people to him: If a mountain had loved me, it would have crumbled down.

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِيُّ: The Ansari, referring to the tribe of Ansar in Medina
key_terms.سَهْلُ بْنُ حُنَيْفٍ: Sahl ibn Hunayf, a companion of the Prophet and Imam Ali
key_terms.صِفِّينَ: Siffin, the site of the battle between Imam Ali and Muawiyah

ai.seo_question: Who was Sahl ibn Hunayf and what was his relationship with Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This narration from Nahj al-Balagha records the death of Sahl ibn Hunayf al-Ansari in Kufah after the Battle of Siffin, highlighting the profound affection Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (AS) held for him. The poetic statement 'If a mountain loved me, it would crumble' serves as a metaphor for the intensity of divine and human love, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the emotional depth of the Ahl al-Bayt's relationships with their companions.
